findings.title: Scope contradiction on 'pure data definitions'
findings.evidence: "This spec has zero state transitions — it is pure data definitions." vs "Epoch rules (enforced by consumers...)", handshake rule with exact string match and WS close, per-tool timeout table, FluentValidation cross-field rules
findings.problem: Document explicitly disclaims behavioral content then embeds rejection rules, lifecycle semantics, timeout values, and validation split that dictate consumer state machines.
findings.why_it_matters: Creates immediate overlap with SPEC-03/SPEC-04 that this document claims to be independent of; downstream specs will duplicate or contradict rules, causing integration failures.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove all behavioral rules, enforcement logic, timeout table and validation policy to a dedicated state or orchestration spec; restrict this document to type shapes and JSON contract only.

findings.title: Brittle co-location assumption for ScreenshotResult
findings.location: Section 7.1 ScreenshotResult and note "Screenshot bytes do NOT travel over the wire. The add-in writes the PNG to a shared directory"
findings.evidence: ScreenshotResult contains "FilePath" and "Sha256Hash"; "See SPEC-02 for the shared-directory convention"
findings.problem: Wire protocol is defined over WebSocket (which supports remote endpoints) yet result type assumes shared filesystem between add-in and orchestrator.
findings.why_it_matters: Breaks if orchestrator runs on different machine, container, or cloud function; forces unstated deployment constraint that contradicts process-boundary premise of the entire spec family.
findings.proposed_fix: Either transmit image bytes (base64 or binary WS message) inside wire contract or explicitly mark remote-filesystem co-location as a hard architectural invariant in Section 0.

findings.title: Unspecified fragmentation protocol for >4 MiB messages
findings.evidence: "Maximum single-message size: 4 MiB. Above this, the sender breaks the payload (e.g., large feature tree) into streamed smaller messages."
findings.problem: No definition of chunk wrapper type, sequencing, correlation to original polymorphic message, completion signal, or error handling; contradicts earlier statement that WS frame reassembly by System.Net.WebSockets is sufficient.
findings.why_it_matters: StateSnapshot and GetFeatureTreeResult easily exceed limit under realistic CAD models; implementations will invent incompatible chunking schemes, breaking the "all other specs reference types defined here and add nothing" guarantee.
findings.proposed_fix: Define explicit ChunkedPayload or ContinuationMessage type in polymorphic families or raise limit and rely exclusively on transport-level fragmentation with clear max size enforcement rules.

findings.title: Complexity inflation via reflection-based completeness tests
findings.location: Sections 4.3, 11 and 15 (JsonDerivedTypeRegistrationCompletenessTests, ToolRegistryCompletenessTests, ToolRegistry static constructor)
findings.evidence: "reflects all concrete implementations of each polymorphic interface in the Protocol assembly and fails the build if any concrete type lacks a [JsonDerivedType] attribute"
findings.problem: Protocol correctness now depends on runtime assembly scanning, attribute presence, and 11 build-breaking tests including FsCheck on 1000 random trees.
findings.why_it_matters: Any rename, split, or addition of a tool outside the exact reflection contract breaks CI; opposite of "pure data definitions"; creates fragile dependency on perfect test environment and .NET reflection semantics.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with explicit static registration list or Roslyn source generator that produces the derived-type attributes and registry from a single source of truth.

top_3_must_fix: Unspecified fragmentation protocol for >4 MiB messages
